title: Reverse Bits
statement:
Reverse the order of the 32 bits of an integer.

Contract
- `value` is any `int`. Think of it as a row of 32 bits where bit 0 is the least significant.
- Return the `int` whose bit `31 - i` equals bit `i` of `value`, for every `i` from `0` to `31`.
- Leading zeros matter: all 32 positions take part, so the result can be negative.

Examples
- `reverseBits(1)` returns `-2147483648` (only the top bit is set).
- `reverseBits(6)` returns `1610612736`, which is `0x60000000`.
- `reverseBits(-1)` returns `-1`.
hints: Pick one bit position and decide where that bit has to end up in the result.
Build the answer in a loop: shift the result left to make room, copy in the lowest bit of the input, then shift the input right. Run exactly 32 times so leading zeros are included.
Use the unsigned shift `>>>` so the sign bit cannot smear into the input. Intended complexity: O(1) per call (32 steps) and O(1) space, so a batch of n calls costs O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
inputSyntax: Input: a single integer, for example: 6
